title: Control menopausal hot flashes through neurokinin-3 receptor blockade

concept.text: Treat moderate-to-severe menopausal vasomotor symptoms through targeted non-hormonal pharmacology. Fezolinetant established this class; subsequent recognition of serious liver-injury risk qualifies its clinical use. Proposed completion test: FDA approval of an NK3 antagonist for menopausal vasomotor symptoms, supported by randomized phase 3 evidence of reduced hot-flash frequency and severity through 12 weeks and longer safety follow-up. Test set by: FDA; pivotal efficacy and safety endpoints were evaluated in the fezolinetant programme. Reported achieved: FDA approved fezolinetant (Veozah) on 12 May 2023; a boxed liver-injury warning was added on 16 December 2024. Overlaps: OBG-05, END-08. Sources given: [FDA fezolinetant approval announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-novel-drug-treat-moderate-severe-hot-flashes-caused-menopause) ; [FDA subsequent liver-injury warning](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-communications/fda-adds-warning-about-rare-occurrence-serious-liver-injury-use-veozah-fezolinetant-hot-flashes-due).

page.title: First FDA-approved NK3 receptor antagonist for menopausal vasomotor symptoms
page.definition: Fezolinetant is an oral, nonhormonal treatment for moderate to severe hot flashes and night sweats due to menopause. It blocks neurokinin B at neurokinin-3 (NK3) receptors on neurons that help regulate body temperature, reducing the frequency and severity of these symptoms.

goal.need: Up to 80% of menopausal women experience hot flashes or night sweats, and symptoms can last more than 10 years in one-third of women. Hormone therapy is the most effective treatment, but some women cannot use it or prefer to avoid it. Low-dose paroxetine offers modest relief. With fezolinetant, women for whom hormone therapy was unsuitable had fewer and less severe episodes and reported less disturbed sleep than with placebo at 24 weeks. Its rare risk of serious liver injury requires blood tests before and during treatment.

milestones.title: An NK3 antagonist has nonclinical evidence supporting human dosing.
milestones.criterion: Laboratory pharmacology and toxicology data support the sponsor’s conclusion that the proposed human investigation is reasonably safe at the intended dose and duration. The scope and duration of nonclinical testing must support the particular investigation proposed.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8); application to fezolinetant documented in the NDA 216578 nonclinical review.
milestones.threshold_quote: reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: An NK3 antagonist reduces hot-flash counts versus placebo after 4 weeks at two-sided P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: In a randomized, double-blind crossover trial in women with menopausal hot flashes, compare the total number of hot flashes during the final week of each 4-week treatment period. The periods are separated by a 2-week washout. The count must be lower with the NK3 antagonist than with placebo at two-sided P<0.05.
milestones.set_by: Imperial College London, protocol MR/M024954/1, registered as EudraCT 2015-001553-32 and NCT02668185.
milestones.threshold_quote: Total Number of Hot Flushes During the Final Week of Both Treatment Periods.

milestones.title: A dose-ranging trial finds an NK3-antagonist regimen improving all four hot-flash endpoints at P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: In a 12-week randomized, placebo-controlled dose-ranging trial, at least one regimen produces greater reductions from baseline than placebo in both frequency and severity of moderate to severe hot flashes at weeks 4 and 12. Each of the four pairwise comparisons must have two-sided P<0.05 without multiplicity adjustment. Daily severity is the mean score per moderate or severe episode, with moderate scored 2 and severe scored 3. A day with neither scores 0. Average the daily scores over seven days.
milestones.set_by: OGEDA/Astellas, VESTA protocol NCT03192176; endpoints and statistical tests reproduced in the published phase 2b report.
milestones.threshold_quote: using a two-sided test at 5% error rate without the multiplicity adjustment.

milestones.title: Two trials show ≥2 fewer daily hot flashes beyond placebo and lower severity at weeks 4 and 12.
milestones.criterion: In each of two randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials, the same dose produces greater reductions from baseline in frequency and severity at both weeks 4 and 12, significant at the 0.05 level after multiplicity adjustment. At each visit the mean reduction in moderate to severe episodes must exceed placebo’s by at least 2 per day. Daily severity averages episode scores of 2 for moderate and 3 for severe at baseline, adding mild episodes scored 1 after baseline. Days with no qualifying episodes score 0.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, development advice and NDA 216578 statistical review; statistical significance level documented in the approved prescribing information.
milestones.threshold_quote: at least 14 moderate to severe VMS per week or 2 moderate to severe VMS per day

milestones.title: At 12 months, endometrial hyperplasia or cancer occurs in ≤1%, with a one-sided 95% upper limit ≤4%.
milestones.criterion: In a 12-month safety assessment of treated postmenopausal women with a uterus, use centrally read biopsies to determine the proportion with endometrial hyperplasia or cancer at the proposed dose. Include evaluable end-of-treatment biopsies and qualifying diagnoses made earlier during treatment. The combined proportion must be ≤1%, and its exact one-sided 95% upper confidence limit must be ≤4%.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, phase 3 endometrial safety advice for NDA 216578 and Veozah prescribing information, section 14.2.
milestones.threshold_quote: ≤ 1% with the upper bound of the one-sided 95% confidence limit being ≤ 4%.

milestones.title: A compound inhibits signaling through the human NK3 receptor in a cell assay.
milestones.criterion: In cells expressing human NK3 receptors, an activating ligand produces a measurable response, and adding the candidate compound reduces that response relative to the ligand alone.
milestones.set_by: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry, functional definition of an antagonist, applied to the human NK3 receptor assay in the FDA nonclinical review.
milestones.threshold_quote: Substance that reverses or reduces the effect induced by an agonist.

milestones.title: Human dosing establishes NK3-antagonist exposure and tolerability sufficient to design a phase 2 trial.
milestones.criterion: In a monitored human study, characterize drug exposure, pharmacological effects, and adverse effects as dose increases sufficiently to design a controlled phase 2 study.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(a)(1).
milestones.threshold_quote: to permit the design of well-controlled, scientifically valid, Phase 2 studies.

milestones.title: The FDA accepts an NK3-antagonist application for substantive review for menopausal symptoms.
milestones.criterion: The FDA files a new drug application seeking approval of an NK3 receptor antagonist for moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause. Filing requires the agency to determine that the application is complete enough for substantive review.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 314.101(a)(1).
milestones.threshold_quote: the NDA is sufficiently complete to permit a substantive review.

results.finding: Fezolinetant inhibited neurokinin A signaling in human NK3 receptor–expressing cells at an IC50 of 12.9–22.0 nmol/L (replicate count unreported).
In the repeat-dose monkey study supporting phase 3, fezolinetant’s no-adverse-effect exposure was 43-fold the human benchmark (group sizes unreported).
results.detail: The monkey no-observed-adverse-effect level was 25 mg/kg/day. At 40 mg/kg/day, severe thrombocytopenia led to hemorrhage and moribundity in one female.
results.quote:
The Division agreed that main 
human metabolite was adequately addressed in these studies 
and these studies supported the proposed duration of the 
Phase 3 clinical trial.

results.finding: In healthy menopausal volunteers given fezolinetant, its main metabolite accounted for approximately 50% of drug-related plasma AUC (sample size unreported).
results.quote:
In human, the major metabolite, ES00259564, was approximately 50% of the total 
fezolinetant-related plasma [AUC] exposure (Table 4).

results.finding: In 37 women with menopausal hot flushes, MLE4901 yielded 29.66 fewer hot flushes than placebo in the final treatment week.
results.quote:
MLE4901 significantly reduced the total weekly number of hot flushes by 45 percentage points (95% CI 22–67) compared with the placebo (intention-to-treat adjusted means: placebo 49·01 [95% CI 40·81–58·56]
vs
MLE4901 19·35 [15·99–23·42]; adjusted estimate of difference 29·66 [17·39–42·87], p<0·0001).

results.finding: Fezolinetant (n=349 in the efficacy analysis) reduced moderate or severe vasomotor symptom frequency by up to 3.5 episodes/day beyond placebo at week 4.
results.quote:
Fezolinetant reduced moderate/severe VMS frequency by −1.9 to −3.5/day at week 4 and −1.8 to −2.6/day at week 12 (all
P <
0.05 vs placebo).

results.finding: Fezolinetant (n=349 in the efficacy analysis) improved all four coprimary endpoints versus placebo with three regimens.
results.detail: For 90 mg twice daily, frequency fell by 3.5 and 2.6 episodes/day beyond placebo at weeks 4 and 12. Severity fell by 1.0 and 0.6 points. The respective nominal P values were <0.0001 and 0.0005 for frequency and <0.0001 and 0.0028 for severity.
results.quote: In the primary analysis, all fezolinetant regimens significantly reduced the severity of moderate/severe VMS relative to placebo at week 4, and fezolinetant 60 mg BID, 90 mg BID, and 60 mg QD significantly reduced VMS severity relative to placebo at week 12

results.finding: Fezolinetant 90 mg twice daily (trial efficacy n=349) reduced week-12 frequency by 2.6 episodes/day beyond placebo.
results.detail: Table 3 gives the dose-specific effects. The primary severity calculation excluded mild episodes throughout.

results.finding: The fezolinetant trial (n=352 treated, including placebo) reported zero clinically significant endometrial biopsy findings.
results.detail: The paper gives no evaluable biopsy denominator by dose.
results.quote: There were no clinically significant endometrial biopsy findings

results.finding: Fezolinetant (n=352 treated, including placebo) produced dose-dependent luteinizing hormone reductions at 3 hours postdose.
results.quote: fezolinetant was associated with dose-dependent LH reductions 3-hours postdose compared with either baseline or predose.

results.finding: In SKYLIGHT 1 (522 women analyzed), fezolinetant 45 mg reduced moderate-to-severe hot flashes by 2.07 episodes per day beyond placebo at week 4.
results.detail: The 30 mg dose fell short of the frequency threshold at week 4. The paper describes SKYLIGHT 2 and cites its sleep result, but provides no second-trial frequency and severity estimates for the four required comparisons.
results.quote:
For frequency of moderate-to-severe vasomotor 
symptoms, compared with placebo, the change in least 
squares means for fezolinetant 30 mg was –1·87 
(SE 0·42; p<0·001) and –2·07 (0·42; p<0·001) for 
fezolinetant 45 mg at week 4.

results.finding: Among 173 women receiving fezolinetant 45 mg, zero events of endometrial hyperplasia, cancer, or disordered proliferative endometrium were recorded during the 12-week controlled period.
results.detail: The denominator is the entire 45 mg safety arm. The paper describes week-52 biopsies in the methods and gives the relevant adverse-event counts only for the 12-week controlled period.

results.finding: In SKYLIGHT 2 (n=500 analyzed), fezolinetant 45 mg reduced moderate to severe hot flashes by 2.53 episodes per day beyond placebo at week 12.
results.detail: The 30-mg dose fell below the 2-episode threshold at both visits, with placebo-adjusted reductions of 1.82 and 1.86 episodes per day.
results.quote: Both fezolinetant doses met statistical significance in reducing VMS frequency and severity/24 hours at weeks 4 and 12 vs placebo with multiplicity adjustment

results.finding: Among 167 women assigned to fezolinetant 45 mg from study start, zero combined endometrial adverse events were recorded through week 52.
results.detail: The safety denominator includes treated women regardless of biopsy evaluability. The adverse-event category also includes disordered proliferative endometrium.

results.finding: At 52 weeks, 0.5% had endometrial hyperplasia or cancer with fezolinetant 45 mg (n=203) and with 30 mg (n=210).
results.detail: The combined endpoint has the same numerator and confidence limit as the sole event category at each dose because the other category had zero events.
results.quote: Endometrial hyperplasia or malignancy in fezolinetant-treated participants, as assessed by centrally read endometrial biopsies in the endometrial health set, was within the FDA’s prespecified limits of 1% or less, with an upper limit of one-sided 95% CI of 4% or less.

results.finding: The FDA approved one NK3 antagonist, Veozah (fezolinetant) 45 mg, for moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause.
results.quote:
It is approved, effective 
on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon 
labeling.

results.finding: Fezolinetant 45 mg in SKYLIGHT 1 and 2 (N=522 and 500) reduced daily moderate to severe hot flashes by at least 2.07 more than placebo.
results.detail: The 30 mg dose fell short of the frequency threshold at week 4 in both trials and at week 12 in SKYLIGHT 2.
results.quote:
for the 45 mg arm, the LS mean differences from placebo was over 2 unit at week 4 and at week 
12 in both studies.

results.finding: In 400 female rats, 65% of the highest-dose ESN364 group survived to terminal necropsy.
results.detail: The reported survival comparison is one endpoint of the carcinogenicity study.
results.quote:
The sponsor’s analysis showed that the numbers of rats surviving to their terminal necropsy were 
59 (59%), 65 (65%), 60 (60%), and 65 (65%) in the vehicle control, the low, mid, and high dose 
groups for female rats, respectively.

results.finding: Fezolinetant in VESTA (n=349): three regimens improved all four frequency and severity endpoints versus placebo.
results.detail: Table 3 gives the individual P values. For 90 mg twice daily, the week 4 and 12 values were <0.0001 and 0.0005 for frequency and <0.0001 and 0.0028 for severity.
results.quote: In the primary analysis, all fezolinetant regimens significantly reduced the severity of moderate/severe VMS relative to placebo at week 4, and fezolinetant 60 mg BID, 90 mg BID, and 60 mg QD significantly reduced VMS severity relative to placebo at week 12

results.finding: Fezolinetant 90 mg twice daily in VESTA (n=349): the smaller frequency advantage across the two visits was 2.6 episodes/day.
VESTA (n=352 treated overall) reported zero clinically significant endometrial biopsy findings over 12 weeks.
results.detail: The safety population includes placebo recipients and is not the biopsy denominator.
results.quote: There were no clinically significant endometrial biopsy findings

results.finding: GS1-144 produced dose-dependent luteinizing hormone reductions across 15–120 mg in the repeat-dose cohort (n=66).
results.detail: The repeat-dose cohort included healthy women of childbearing potential and postmenopausal women who received GS1-144 or placebo for seven days. The authors support further clinical development of GS1-144 for menopausal vasomotor symptoms.
results.quote: Dose-dependent LH reductions were observed across 15-120 mg, with consistent effects between 30 mg q12h and 60 mg q24h (MAD).

results.finding: Fezolinetant 45 mg (n=683 across dose and placebo arms) reduced moderate to severe hot flashes by at least 2.07 more per day than placebo at both visits in both trials.
results.detail: Tables 2 and 3 establish the efficacy comparisons. The supplied text leaves the specified daily severity calculation unverified.

results.finding: The FDA accepted one fezolinetant NDA for substantive review for moderate to severe menopausal vasomotor symptoms, effective 60 days after receipt.
results.detail: The FDA classified the application for Priority Review.
results.quote:
We have completed our filing review and have determined that your application is
sufficiently complete to permit a substantive review. Therefore, in accordance with 21
CFR 314.101(a), this application is considered filed 60 days after the date we received
your application.
